name: TX-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 13 points, and the open seat keeps fundamentals firmly red
Overwhelming money gap: Steinmann raised $2.4M with $1.7M outside support versus $30K for Jones
Prediction markets price the Democratic win chance at about 4 percent
No public polling or expert ratings, which widens uncertainty around the margin
model.rationale: The district's 13-point Republican lean, an 80-to-1 fundraising gap in Steinmann's favor, and $1.7 million in outside support outweigh any advantage Democrats might gain from Luttrell's retirement. Markets give Democrats about a 4 percent chance, and nothing in the evidence points to a closer race.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a sharp national shift toward Democrats would be the most plausible route to a tighter contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's 8th District leans Republican by 13 points, and Morgan Luttrell's retirement has not changed the basic shape of the race. Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann enters the general election with roughly $2.4 million raised and $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised under $30,000 with no reported outside spending. Prediction markets give Democrats about a 4 percent chance of taking the seat.

No public general-election polling exists, which adds uncertainty to the precise margin, but the available signals all point the same way. The open seat removes a modest incumbency advantage for Republicans, yet the district's lean, the financial imbalance, and market pricing make a Democratic upset unlikely. The forecast expects the seat to remain in Republican hands.
